concept.name: Ice
concept.definition: A Wyckoff metaphor for the zone of support at the lower boundary of a distribution trading range, defined by the lows of the reactions within the range. Price that breaks decisively through it has 'fallen through the ice', marking the transition to markdown.
concept.intuition: Support is pictured as a frozen surface holding the market up; once it cracks, price plunges into the water below.
concept.mechanics: The ice is drawn at the lows of the reactions in the range (often simplified to the range's support level, though it can sit higher up depending on where reaction lows cluster). A fall through the ice on wide downside spreads and high volume confirms supply dominance; a subsequent feeble rally back toward the ice zone is treated as a prime short-entry area.
concept.failure_modes: Ice is a zone, not a precise line, so penetrations without the characteristic wide spread and volume may be shakeouts rather than genuine breaks; a quick recovery back above the ice negates the breakdown reading.
concept.misconceptions: The ice is not always identical to the range's lowest support line — it is defined by the cluster of reaction lows — and the term is metaphorical shorthand rather than a formally defined event.
concept.example: A distribution range's reaction lows cluster at 136-138, which the analyst marks as the ice; a high-volume drop to 130 is a fall through the ice, and the weak bounce to 137 is shorted.

citations.source: Primary Selling Opportunity - Rally Back to the Ice (Last Point of Supply) (Wyckoff Stock Market Institute)
